question.worked_solution:
The integral is defined over a type I region.

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{x+2}4x\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{1}^{2}4x[{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{x+2}\,dy]dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}4x[\,y\,]_{{x}^{2}}^{x+2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}4x(x+2-{x}^{2})\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}(4{x}^{2}+8x-4{x}^{3})\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}(4{x}^{2}+8x-4{x}^{3})\,dx & ={[\frac{4{x}^{3}}{3}+4{x}^{2}-{x}^{4}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =(\frac{32}{3}+16-16)-(\frac{4}{3}+4-1) \\  & =\frac{32}{3}-\frac{13}{3} \\  & =\frac{19}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
